reason: Camera pivot behaviour for the 3D map is a durable design rule (the orbit target stays on the selected node). Future camera, wheel or selection changes must not undo it, and no existing skill covers the orbit camera.

The live skill says the pivot ends on flyTo and never says what happens when a hand cuts a selection flight short. The trace shows the code path (flight.js flyTo calls pivotEnds; fly3d.js flights pass done: pivotOn) and an in-tree fix that adds PIVOT.pending and a steer3d start handler, so the rule the skill should carry is that gap and its fix.
The trace shows the browser test needed an empty-stage drag, a settle before the read, and a without-fix check on a copy. None of that was in the skill.

Reviewer found the click path to a figure bypasses the follow clearance and the pivot dollies the camera into a large unlimited figure. The pivot skill is the one in play and governs this exact behaviour, so the rule belongs here with its verifying test.
The follow clearance direction and measurement point were wrong and are now fixed; the skill that covers 3D camera clearance must state the rule, or the next edit reverts it.

Current followIn3d floor is a ratchet, and a first-frame dip into a large figure is still open; the existing skill describes the floor but not that gap or the limited-size distance. Dated so a later agent can tell whether the hard floor has landed.
The episode showed a thin-margin camera test that looked passing on one run and needed repeated runs; that rerun rule and the copy-aside check are not in the skill yet.
The open gap in this skill now has a verified cause: orbit-control damping drifts the camera before followIn3d first runs. Future clearance work should start from the cause, not re-investigate it.
